back: Waves exploit a joint → cave → eroded through → arch → roof collapses → stack → undercut → stump.
Notch at the cliff base → overhang collapses → cliff retreats → gently sloping platform left, exposed at low tide.
Discordant coast: weak rock eroded into bays; resistant rock left as headlands.
Rock bands parallel to the coast; fairly straight; coves where the outer band is breached (Lulworth Cove).
Rock bands at right angles to the coast; alternating headlands and bays (Swanage Bay).
Longshore drift continues past a change in coastline direction; deposition in calm water; recurved end; salt marsh behind.
Ridge of sediment across a bay joining two headlands, trapping a lagoon (Slapton Sands).
Embryo dunes → yellow (fore) dunes bound by marram grass → grey dunes → dune slacks.
Durdle Door (arch), Old Harry Rocks (stack and stump), Spurn Head (spit), Slapton Sands (bar).
